title: Separate the checkpoint load out of TabDPTEstimator.__init__
body:
## Summary

`TabDPTEstimator.__init__` downloads (or reads) the checkpoint and builds `self.model` inline, so there is no way for a caller to reuse an already-built network across several estimators, or to substitute one for testing, without re-implementing the constructor. We hit this while running TabDPT-Turbo as part of a benchmark (a bagged ensemble fits several estimators from the same checkpoint per process, and rebuilding the network for each one dominates the fit time), and worked around it with a constructor replica kept in sync by hand. This PR extracts the load into `_load_model()`, a method the constructor calls once, so overriding or monkeypatching that single method is enough.

## What changed

- `TabDPTEstimator._load_model(self)`: the checkpoint resolution (`model_weight_path` or `download_weights()`), the `safetensors` read and `TabDPTModel.load(...)` call, exactly as they were in `__init__`, just moved into their own method.
- `__init__` now stores `clip_sigma` and `model_weight_path` on `self` before calling `_load_model()`. They were previously read only as local constructor variables, which means `TabDPTEstimator(...).get_params()` raised `AttributeError` for every instance (sklearn's `BaseEstimator` contract requires every constructor argument to be readable back off `self`); this is a pre-existing bug, fixed as a side effect of the extraction.

No other behavior changes: the constructor's signature, defaults, and validation are unchanged, `TabDPTClassifier`/`TabDPTRegressor` (which just forward to `super().__init__`) are unaffected, and the existing test suite passes without modification.

## Tests

Ran the full existing suite (`tests/test_estimator.py`, `test_cls.py`, `test_reg.py`, `test_utils.py`, `device_utils.py`; `test_inference.py` needs GPU hardware not available here) against the real Hugging Face checkpoint: 40 passed, unmodified. Added three tests to `test_estimator.py`:

- `test_load_model_is_separately_callable`: `_load_model()` can be called again after construction and rebuilds the network.
- `test_load_model_can_be_overridden_to_share_a_network`: a subclass overriding `_load_model()` can hand back an already-built module instead of loading its own, the seam this PR is for.
- `test_get_params_reads_every_constructor_argument`: `get_params()` now returns `clip_sigma` and `model_weight_path`.

title: Always use inf_batch_size during inference, even without retrieval
body:
Ensures we don't OOM on very large test sets. Downside is that it'll slow down inference when retrieval isn't used.

Also use inf_batch_size on CPU when explicitly specified, and warn user to set it explicitly instead of silently overriding with a really low and slow value (this has made it look unexpectedly slow for me when testing on CPU before).

Also get rid of the last `squeeze()` without a dim specified.

In a future update, we should do the following breaking change, since memory usage is `O(context_size + inf_batch_size)` without retrieval but `O(context_size * inf_batch_size)` with retrieval:
- Move inf_batch_size to be a predict parameter
- If `None`, set the default based on both the device and whether retrieval is used, suggested values:
    - GPU+No retrieval: 1M
    - GPU+Retrieval: 512
    - CPU+No Retrieval:  32k
    - CPU+Retrieval: 16

Probably only needs 1 review, whoever's free.

title: Align n_ensembles handling between classifier predict functions
body:
Allows using TabDPTClassifier.ensemble_predict_proba as a single entry point for probabilistic outputs, matching the behaviour of predict(). This will affect inference behaviour slightly, but only slightly for an unusual case (using ensemble_predict_proba with n_ensembles==1 will no longer shuffle columns)

For a future major update, we could consider exposing this behaviour for predict_proba, more closely matching sklearn expectations, but it might be too risky a change for existing code.

title: [CRITICAL BUG] TabDPT returns inconsistent dimensions for binary when predicting on a single sample.
body:
Note: I have opened #64 which resolves the issue. I would request the authors to release v1.1.12 after merging to propagate the fix to AutoGluon 1.5.

In binary classification, TabDPT returns a different output dimension depending on if it is predicting on 1 sample vs multiple samples, despite in both cases taking a np.ndarray as input.

```python
print(X.shape)  # (2, 14)
y_pred_proba = model.ensemble_predict_proba(X)
print(y_pred_proba.shape)  # (2, 2)

X_single = X[:1, :]
print(X_single.shape)  # (1, 14)
y_pred_proba_single = model.ensemble_predict_proba(X_single)
print(y_pred_proba_single.shape)  # (2,)
```

The cause is due to this line in `predict_proba`:

```
pred_val = pred.float().squeeze().detach().cpu().numpy()
```

In the case where there are 2 samples, the input dimensions are (2, 1, N), and squeeze turns it into (2, N) -> 2d
In the case where there is 1 sample, the input dimensions are (1, 1, N), and squeeze turns it into (N,) -> 1d

I discovered this bug during some testing with AutoGluon where I noticed AutoGluon crashed if asked to predict on a single sample when TabDPT was part of the ensemble. Currently any ensemble that includes TabDPT will crash at inference time if asked to predict a single sample for binary classification.

For example:

```python
# AutoGluon 1.5
predictor = TabularPredictor(...).fit(..., hyperparameters={"TABDPT": {}})
predictor.predict_proba(test_data.head(1))  # <-- crashes
```

This edge-case was previously overlooked in AutoGluon's automated testing for each model. I have since added a check for this so in future we will catch this issue before release.


# Fix

To fix the bug, we can edit the TabDPTClassifier `predict_proba` method:

```
return pred_val
```

To instead be:

```
# Ensure pred_val is always (n_samples, n_classes) even for a single sample.
if pred_val.ndim == 1:
    pred_val = pred_val[None, :]  # (n_classes,) -> (1, n_classes)
return pred_val
```

title: Add a `model.to(device)` method
body:
It would be awesome if TabDPT implemented a `model.to(device)` method such that the user can toggle between cpu and CUDA backends.

For example, this is how AutoGluon is leveraging this `model.to(device)` logic for RealMLP to enable CPU inference and CPU model loading: https://github.com/autogluon/autogluon/pull/5434/commits/c9406204ffae47fc60728c3427df145a39e96c98

Without this method, TabDPT wouldn't be loadable on a CPU only machine if it were saved on a GPU machine, because the weights would be saved with CUDA device.

I think this would roughly be the last ask I have for enabling TabDPT in the AG 1.5 release, everything else appears to be working.

This PR includes two small changes to improve the regression interface. 

First, I added a default value for `context_size`, the same as for classification.

Second, I fixed an error in the case where the context was larger than the training data. Previously, this would cause an error `unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'numpy.ndarray' and 'Tensor'` as the predictions were transformed to numpy before being multiplied with a torch tensor.
